gen-gf-delius-unicase-gf-noto-sans-kharo: Noto Sans Kharoshthi lays down a thick, dark band of lowercase, with curves that never quite close. Delius Unicase is the loose, hand-drawn one, tube-smooth and relaxed, while the body is the one that holds a line together.
gen-gf-delius-unicase-gf-noto-sans-khmer: Cut-from-a-strip strokes of one width give Delius Unicase its handwritten, tube-smooth look, while Noto Sans Khmer keeps its small letters tall and its openings generous. Make the heading small or the body large, and that difference softens.
gen-gf-delius-unicase-gf-noto-sans-khuda: Loose, handwritten, friendly. Delius Unicase draws every stroke without any swing from heavy to light, and Noto Sans Khudawadi sits beneath it as a sans with hooked rounds left unlatched and capitals barely taller than the rest.
gen-gf-delius-unicase-gf-noto-sans-kr: No thick-and-thin shifts anywhere in Delius Unicase, just a handwritten line with a pronounced x-height and rope-ladder spacing. But Noto Sans KR is the one built for text, with generous gaps in its curves and stubby ascenders under a big x-height.
gen-gf-delius-unicase-gf-noto-sans-lao: Delius Unicase is handwritten with a monoline skeleton, relaxed and inviting, its strokes never tapering at the ends. Noto Sans Lao brings a sans body with a very high x-height, and that mix of loose pen and open, tall text is the pair's best quality.
gen-gf-delius-unicase-gf-noto-sans-lao-l: Noto Sans Lao Looped makes words look like solid blocks, not skylines. Its bowls stay unfinished on one side, and under Delius Unicase's constant, handwritten stroke that gives the pair a friendly, modern feel.
gen-gf-delius-unicase-gf-noto-sans-lepch: Noto Sans Lepcha reads with wide-open curves and a lowercase as sturdy as cast iron capitals. Delius Unicase, handwritten and relaxed, joins stems and connecting strokes without any modulation, and that gap in character is what makes the pair stand out.
gen-gf-delius-unicase-gf-noto-sans-limbu: Noto Sans Limbu has tall-bodied small letters and curves that gape wide open. Delius Unicase, handwritten and monoline, hands over to a body that would read as easy, upright and friendly across a longer passage.
gen-gf-delius-unicase-gf-noto-sans-lisu: Relaxed and inviting, Delius Unicase writes like toothpaste squeezed in one steady line. Noto Sans Lisu is the plain sans underneath, with tiny gaps below its ascender tops and wide-open s curves, and the handwritten-meets-tidy contrast is the pair's best quality.
gen-gf-delius-unicase-gf-noto-sans-lydia: Every glyph in Delius Unicase looks drawn with a single pen tip, handwritten and relaxed. Noto Sans Lydian, a plain sans with capitals barely taller than lowercase and a paper-clip-wide opening, would read smoothly and approachably over a longer passage.
